newsitem.title: USA: Key U.S. meat packer operations slowed by weather.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. meat packer operations slowed by weather.

text.p: Operations at some major U.S. meat packing operations in the Midwest were slowed by frigid, windy weather which hampered transport of livestock, company officials said.
An IBP Inc official Thursday said there was no first shift at its beef plants Thursday in Joslin, Ill. or Laverne, Minn., due to adverse weather in those areas.

IBP spokesman, Gary Mickelson, also said there was no information available yet regarding if the weather would affect later shifts on Thursday or Friday operations at the Illinois and Minnesota beef plants.
Further, there was no word on how weather has affected IBP's seven pork plants, five of which are in Iowa, Mickelson said.

Conagra Inc. unit Swift and Co. pork plants in Worthington, Minn. and Marshalltown, Iowa were late getting started, said K.T. Miller, company spokeswoman. Miller said she did not have information on Conagra's three Monfort beef plants.

A company official with John Morrell and Co, a unit of Smithfield Foods Inc, said its two pork plants at Sioux Falls, S.D. and Sioux City, Iowa would only operate one shift because of restricted hog movement.
"We will be down quite a bit in numbers because of the weather," the company official said.

Trade sources said Dakota Industries' American Foods Group Huron, S.D. pork plant was not operating. Company officials at corporate headquarters in Green Bay, Wis., were unable to confirm the closing.
Cargill Inc unit Excel Corp spokesman Mark Klein said the company did not have weather-related information yet on its Midwestern beef and pork plants.
Hog slaughter conducted under federal inspection Thursday was estimated by livestock analysts at 225,000 to 275,000 head compared with 325,000 a week ago and 288,000 a year ago.
